newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Kaucuk agrees merger ratio.
newsitem.headline: Czech Kaucuk agrees merger ratio.

text.p: Shareholders of Czech petrochemical conglomerate Kaucuk Group a.s. on Thursday agreed to a merger plan which swaps Kaucuk stock at a ratio of one-to- 1.2 shares of Unipetrol a.s., a company official told Reuters.
The general meeting also approved a net dividend of 10 crowns per share on 1996 profit, unchanged from the previous year.

The plan completes a three-way merger joining Kaucuk and Unipetrol with Chemopetrol a.s., as one under the Unipetrol title, as part of the government's petrochemical privatisation plan, which separated refinery assets into a separate company.
The swap entails an exchange of 12 shares of Unipetrol, with a nominal value of 100 crowns each, with one Kaucuk share worth a nominal 1,000 crowns.
With Chemopetrol it swaps 11 shares at a nominal 100 crowns for one 1,000 crown Chemopetrol share.
Chemopetrol shareholders earlier on Thursday gave their approval to the plan, and a Unipetrol general meeting later today is expected to do so as well.
Unipetrol shares are still 100 percent held by the Czech government until the merger is complete.
Unipetrol controls fuels distribution company Benzina, as well as the 51 percent of the refining company Ceska Rafinerska.
A consortium of Conoco, Agip SpA, and Royal Dutch/Shell took the remaining 49 percent stake in Rafinerska in 1995.
